clue.text: Delighted to get mark of approval — came first

parts.note: a tick is the mark a teacher puts by a right answer
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to get a teacher's approving mark after finishing top.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tickled is an informal way of being pleased or amused, a close synonym.

clue.text: Woman's hair not right

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is': Woman is the answer

indicators.note: not says the following piece is left out of the word before it

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A remark that some woman's hairdo is not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is just 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tess is a woman's first name, as in Hardy's heroine Tess of the d'Urbervilles.

clue.text: Star is able to work

parts.note: can means is able
an opus is a work, especially a musical composition

explanation.surface: Praise of a celebrity who is capable of doing the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopus is a bright star in the southern constellation Carina, so an example of a star.

clue.text: Sound made by degenerate northerners

indicators.note: says the word for degenerate is said aloud, and the answer is spelt differently

parts.note: to lapse is to slip back or degenerate

explanation.surface: A noise made by some debased people from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapps are the Sami people of Lapland, in the far north of Scandinavia, hence northerners.

clue.text: Chemical in drug needing a bit of time to be absorbed

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken inside, so these pieces go within the drug word

parts.note: dope is slang for a drug
taken as written
MIN is the abbreviation for minute, a short bit of time

explanation.surface: A substance in a narcotic takes a little while to soak in.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopamine is a chemical messenger in the brain, a neurotransmitter.

clue.text: Piano skill — the thing needed with a musical piece

parts.note: P, for piano (softly), is the musical abbreviation
art means skill, as in the art of conversation
it stands for the thing being talked about

explanation.surface: A pianist's skill is the key requirement for a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A partita is a Baroque instrumental suite, so a kind of musical piece.

clue.text: March exhibition

definitions.meaning: to march in procession, as troops do

explanation.definitionFit: To parade is to march in order, and a parade is also a display put on for show.

clue.text: Respect and submissiveness new head demanded

indicators.note: the first letter of the word must be swapped for a different one

parts.note: deference is humble submission to another's wishes

explanation.surface: Respect and obedience are what a new boss insists on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Respect' reads as a noun of esteem, but it is the sense in 'with respect to'; the new head is R, replacing D.
explanation.definitionFit: In respect of and with reference to mean the same, so reference here means regard or relation.

clue.text: Bill's favoured mode of utterance

parts.note: to be in with someone is to be in favour
a voice is the manner in which someone speaks

explanation.surface: A remark on the way a man named Bill likes to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name, but it is the invoice; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill listing goods or services and the amount owed.

clue.text: Catholic feast that's taken for granted

definitions.meaning: the feast on 15 August marking Mary being taken up into heaven

explanation.definitionFit: The Assumption is a Catholic feast day, and an assumption is something supposed without proof.

clue.text: Bird making Australian abrasive?

indicators.note: an Australian accent turns the long a sound towards a long i, so the word is heard as said there

parts.note: sandpaper is an abrasive paper for smoothing wood

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about a bird that produces gritty paper down under.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke relies on the Australian accent, in which 'paper' is said rather like 'piper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpiper is a small wading bird of shores and mudflats.

clue.text: At least ten needed for this ball game?

definitions.text: At least ten needed for this ball game?

parts.words: At least ten needed for this ball game?
parts.note: the game's name is a plural of a number, and two of that number already make ten; it is played by hitting a ball with the hand

explanation.surface: A question about how many players a ball game requires.
explanation.definitionFit: Fives is a British court game in which a ball is struck with the gloved hand against walls.

clue.text: Artistic movement promotes minds that are devious

indicators.note: devious things take a twisting path, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An art movement advertises cunning thinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Postmodernism is a late-20th-century movement in art, architecture and criticism.

clue.text: Location in Isle of Wight where you'd find roach

definitions.meaning: a village and bay on the west of the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast
the roach is a fish of rivers and lakes, not the sea

explanation.definitionFit: Freshwater is an Isle of Wight village, and roach live in fresh water rather than salt.

clue.text: Gentle sound in street drowned by pro-. nouncement

indicators.note: something drowned is covered over, so the street piece goes inside

parts.note: the clue's broken word is pronouncement; a ruling is an official pronouncement

explanation.surface: A soft noise in the road lost under an official declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'pro-. nouncement' is the word pronouncement split by a line break.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustling is the soft crackling sound of leaves or paper moving.

clue.text: Thrashed at that point, overwhelmed by top performer

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so this piece sits inside the next

parts.note: the lead is the principal actor or performer
there means at that place or point

explanation.surface: A star performer swamps someone who was beaten at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathered is British slang for beaten hard, as if with a leather strap.

clue.text: Design of home, temporary accommodation

parts.note: being in means being at home
a tent is a shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: Plans for a house and a short-term place to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent means purpose or aim, as design does in 'by design'.

clue.text: Observed hugging maiden in club's space below stairs

indicators.note: the built piece is placed inside the club word

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games such as cricket

indicators.note: a word hugging another wraps around it

parts.note: seen means observed
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl was spotted being embraced in a club's room below the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space below stairs' sounds like servants' quarters in a grand house; here it is simply the cellar storey.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the storey below ground level, below the stairs of a house.

clue.text: Dividing membrane's secure part fixed in

definitions.note: a possessive phrase, matching an adjective meaning of a septum

indicators.note: a piece fixed in another is set inside it

parts.note: to seal is to secure or fasten shut

explanation.surface: A partition of tissue holds a safely sealed component.
explanation.definitionFit: Septal means relating to a septum, the membrane or wall dividing two cavities.

clue.text: Something creepy in House, with Gladstone seen about?

definitions.text: Something creepy in House, with Gladstone seen about?

indicators.note: a word placed about another goes round it

parts.note: Gladstone was a Victorian Prime Minister, a PM

indicators.note: the insect goes inside the house abbreviation

parts.note: an ant is a creepy-crawly

explanation.surface: A ghostly figure haunts the Commons where Gladstone was seen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a ghost said to haunt Parliament, where Gladstone once sat.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is a ghost, the creepy spectre of a Victorian statesman in the House.

clue.text: Rebel against monarch given little room in battle

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
loo is British slang for a toilet, the little room

explanation.surface: An uprising against the crown in a cramped space during a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo is the 1815 battle in which Napoleon was finally defeated.

clue.text: Cutting school

definitions.meaning: making an incision, as with a lance
a well-known boarding school in West Sussex, England

explanation.definitionFit: Lancing means cutting open, as of a boil, and Lancing College is an English public school.

clue.text: Having power, I respectfully disagree with lifting punishment

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the letters, so they read upwards

parts.note: a polite refusal is 'no, sir'

explanation.surface: Someone in authority politely objects to a lifting of a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Prison, a term inside, is a form of punishment.

clue.text: Awful heat? Beware, then — not hard to get affected by elements

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters of these words are scrambled, less the letter that 'not hard' tells us to drop

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A warning about terrible heat, with advice not to be hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' removes H (the pencil-grade abbreviation) from the jumble of HEAT BEWARE THEN before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather-beaten means worn and roughened by wind, rain and sun, the elements.

clue.text: Diamonds etc, left on the table?

definitions.text: Diamonds etc, left on the table?

parts.words: Diamonds etc, left on the table?
parts.note: card suits such as diamonds remaining in the undealt pile on the table after a deal

explanation.surface: A question about jewels abandoned on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the talon is the stock of cards left over after dealing.

clue.text: Catcall making joker lose heart

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letters go

parts.note: a jester is a court joker

explanation.surface: A heckler's whistle makes a comedian despair.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeer is a mocking shout, much like a catcall from an audience.

clue.text: Old warrior cheers king

parts.note: ta-ta and cheers are both informal British ways of saying goodbye
R stands for Rex, king

explanation.surface: An ancient fighter toasts the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tatars were Turkic warriors who rode with the Mongol hordes, hence an old warrior.

clue.text: Saint —- what he never suffers is an experience of war

parts.note: a saint would never suffer the flames of hell

explanation.surface: A holy man escapes damnation, yet suffers in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellfire is artillery bombardment, part of the experience of war.

clue.text: Hindu incarnation seen by Jewish tribe — Muslims observe this

parts.note: Rama is an incarnation of the god Vishnu
Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: Different faiths side by side, with Muslims keeping their observance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month of fasting that Muslims observe.

clue.text: A bird and a horse occupying territory

indicators.note: an occupying piece takes up position inside another

parts.note: TER is an abbreviation for territory
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A bird and a horse are settled on someone's land.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanager is a brightly coloured American songbird.
